## Summary

I implemented the GOLD membership tier rule with minimal structural impact, following the codebase's existing transient-field pattern (the same one used for `namesakeCount` and `bulkSignupWarning`):

1. **`Owner.java`** — added a `@Transient householdSize` field with a simple getter/setter, keeping each new method at complexity 1.

2. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — added a single line that stores the post-create household size (existing same-household owners in the already-loaded `owners` collection, plus the new owner), reusing the existing `HouseholdMatcher.sameHousehold` helper rather than adding new counting logic.

3. **`OwnerMapper`** — extended the one `membershipTier` expression line to prefer `"GOLD"` when `householdSize >= 3`, otherwise falling through unchanged to the existing SILVER/BRONZE decision.

No new classes, no changes to `addOwner`'s branching structure beyond the one predicate, and the mapper edit stays a single line. The three touched files each get small, cohesive changes, and the GOLD determination is computed once at create time (where the household collection is already in scope) and read back at GET time via the persisted-in-session transient field — exactly how the existing tier inputs already flow.

The test `coreGoldForThreeMemberHousehold` passes (the third shared-household member returns `GOLD`), and the full suite is green.
